standard.title: Agro Textiles — High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Laminated Woven Lay Flat Tube for Use in Mains and Submains of Drip Irrigation System — Specification
standard.sector: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agro-tech

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard prescribes constructional, performance and other requirements for high density polyethylene (HDPE) laminated woven lay flat tube for use in mains and submains of drip irrigation system. These lay flat tubes are not suitable for use in sprinkler system.
standard.scope: This standard prescribes constructional, performance and other requirements for high density polyethylene (HDPE) laminated woven lay flat tube for use in mains and submains of drip irrigation system. These lay flat tubes are not suitable for use in sprinkler system.

version.current_version: First Edition, 2017 (incorporating all preceding systemic and structural review alignments) [1]

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (Agrotech QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all HDPE laminated woven lay flat tubes supplied for mains and submains of drip irrigation systems must conform to IS 16627 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or distributing non-certified lay flat tubes for drip mains/submains is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic agricultural irrigation piping.
requirements: Every roll of certified drip main or submain lay flat tube may be marked with the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards.

The multi-layer laminated HDPE woven fabric is folded and sealed into the lay flat tube using a heat sealing process. To ensure structural seam integrity, the minimum heat-sealed overlap must be strictly maintained at 30 mm.
The internal diameter of the lay flat tube must be measured using a suitable conical plug gauge.

The proof pressure must be reached within a tight time window of 15 to 30 seconds. The tube must hold this proof pressure for 5 minutes without showing any signs of leakage, sweating, or joint warping.

Puncture resistance is evaluated as per Annex C. A specimen of laminated HDPE fabric (minimum 100 mm diameter) is clamped in a circular fixture. A solid steel rod (diameter 8 ± 0.01 mm with a flat end and a 45° × 0.8 mm chamfered edge) is plunged into the fabric to measure the peak puncture resistance in N.

Under Annex E, specimens bowed in the shape of a loop (loop section subjected to folding is 40 mm, secure clamp length is 10 mm on each end, width is 15 mm) are conditioned in a cooling chamber at –5°C. They are subjected to a sudden folding impact from a free-falling metal cylinder mass of 500 g (diameter 18 mm to 29 mm with slightly rounded lower edges). The specimen must not break or show damage.

Under Annex F, test pieces connected in a straight condition with standard fluid and ambient conditioning temperatures must withstand 10,000 pressure impulse cycles under standard test circuits to verify resistance against hydraulic surges.

Each commercial lay flat tube roll must be legibly marked with: a) Name and address of the manufacturer; b) Nominal bore; c) Type of lay flat tube; d) Length in m; f) Batch No. or Lot No.; and f) Month and year of manufacture.
